lines: Mission Control here. The launch pad lights are out and the lunar mice are throwing a party in the dark.
Your job: get one bulb glowing. We will play first and talk after.

toy.prompt: Tap the switch. Watch the bulb.

1: You just closed a gap. That let electricity run round a loop, and the bulb lit up.
A loop like that is called a [[circuit]]. Break the loop and everything stops.
The [[battery]] gives the push. The [[switch]] opens and closes the gap. The [[bulb]] shows you it is working.
2: Closing the switch completed the [[circuit]], so current could flow through the [[bulb]].
The [[battery]] supplies the [[voltage]] (the push). The flow is the [[current]]. The bulb's [[resistance]] decides how much flows.
3: A [[circuit]] must be a complete conducting loop. The [[switch]] controls whether it is closed.
Conventional current leaves the + terminal of the [[battery]], passes through the [[bulb]] and returns to −. [[voltage]], [[current]] and [[resistance]] are linked by one equation, coming next.

help.1: Think of a bike chain. If the chain is joined into a loop, the wheel turns. If there is a gap, nothing moves. A circuit is the chain.
help.2: Picture a toy train track. The train only runs if the track is a full loop. Electricity is the train.
help.3: Tap the switch on, then off, and say out loud what changed. Closed switch, full loop, bulb on.
help.4: Watch: switch off, loop has a gap, bulb dark. Switch on, loop is complete, bulb glows. Now you make it dark again.

intro.1: Here is a rule that links push, flow and squeeze. It goes in your Formula Book, so you never have to remember it.
intro.2: Ohm's law links [[voltage]], [[current]] and [[resistance]]. It goes in your Formula Book.
intro.3: Ohm's law, V = IR. Rearrange it for whichever quantity you need. It goes in your Formula Book.

1: A 6 V battery pushes electricity through a part that squeezes with 2 Ω.
We want the flow. The rule: I = V ÷ R.
That makes 3 A. Three amps flow.
3: Given V = 6 V and R = 2 Ω, find I.
Rearrange V = IR to I = V ÷ R.

prompt.1: A {V} V battery pushes electricity through a part with a squeeze of {R} Ω. How many amps flow?
prompt.2: A {V} V battery pushes electricity through a part with a squeeze of {R} Ω. How many amps flow?
prompt.3: A {V} V battery drives current through a {R} Ω part. Find the current in milliamps (mA).

explain.3: I = V ÷ R = {V} ÷ {R} = {A} A, which is {answer} mA.

wrong.why: That is {V} × {R}. Flow is push ÷ squeeze, so divide.

hints: Which rule gives flow? Look in your Formula Book.
I = V ÷ R. What are V and R here?
V is {V} and R is {R}. So I = {V} ÷ {R}.

help.1: Flow is push divided by squeeze.
help.2: Share the push between the squeeze: like sharing sweets between friends.
help.3: Same idea, different numbers: 8 V and 2 Ω gives 8 ÷ 2 = 4 A. Now do yours.
help.4: Watch: I = V ÷ R. Put your two numbers in, divide, add the unit. Then try again.

stages.title: Light the launch pad

scenarios.story: The pad lights are dead. Build a circuit that makes the bulb glow.
The cockpit lamp is out and a lunar mouse is chewing the manual. Get the lamp glowing.
The airlock light has gone dark. Fix it before the mice find the snacks.

training.text: Training: the parts are already on the board. Close the switch to finish the loop.

standard.text: Build it from nothing: a battery, a switch and a bulb in one full loop, and get the bulb glowing.

stretch.text: Stretch: now light two bulbs at once. Same battery.

hints: Electricity needs a full circle. Is there a gap?
Tap the + dot on the battery, then a dot on the switch. Keep joining parts until you are back at the battery's − dot.
Battery + to the switch, switch to the bulb, bulb back to the battery −. Then tap the switch to close it.

help.1: A circuit is a loop. Join the parts in a ring: battery, switch, bulb, and back to the battery.
help.2: Make a ring like a necklace. Every part is a bead and the wires are the string.
help.3: Example: battery + → switch → bulb → battery −. Then tap the switch to close it.
help.4: Switch to Training. The parts are already there, so all you do is close the switch. Then come back and build your own.

lines: The bulb lit because you made a full loop: battery, switch, bulb, and back.
Open the switch and the loop breaks. No loop, no flow, no light.
Next time: why an LED needs a resistor so it does not retire early.

stages.title: Say hello
stages.task: Your first line of code. print() makes the computer say something. Change the message to greet Mission Control, then run it.
stages.starter:
# Change the message, then run it
print("Hello, Mission Control")
hints: The words go inside the brackets, between quote marks.

help.1: print() shows words on the screen.
help.2: It is like the robot's voice. Whatever is in the quotes, it says.
help.3: print("Hi") says Hi. Try print("Rover online").
help.4: Copy the starter code and run it. Then change the words.

prompt.1: A part carries {I} A of flow from a {V} V battery. What is its squeeze (resistance) in ohms?
prompt.2: A part carries {I} A of flow from a {V} V battery. What is its squeeze (resistance) in ohms?
prompt.3: A part carries {I} mA from a {V} V battery. Find its resistance in ohms.

wrong.why: That multiplies. To find squeeze, divide: R = V ÷ I.

hints: Rearrange V = I × R to get R on its own.

prompt.1: A part has a squeeze of {R} Ω and {I} A flows through it. How many volts of push does it use?
prompt.2: A part has a squeeze of {R} Ω and {I} A flows through it. How many volts of push does it use?
prompt.3: A {R} Ω part carries {I} mA. What voltage is across it, in volts?

wrong.why: That divides. Push = flow × squeeze, so multiply.

hints: V = I × R is straight from the Formula Book.

questions.prompt: A robot part uses {mA} mA. How many amps is that?

wrong.why: That goes the wrong way. mA are small, so the number of amps is smaller: divide by 1000.

hints: Amps are bigger, so you need fewer of them. Divide.
